newsitem.title: USA: Unocal sets $1.34 capital spending in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Unocal sets $1.34 capital spending in 1997.

text.p: Unocal Corp said Monday it was forecasting $1.34 billion in capital expenditures in 1997, versus $1.38 billion for 1996.
The company said two-thirds of its 1997 capital spending budget would be for overseas projects.

In 1995 about 70 percent of capital spending, or more than $1 billion, went to domestic projects, it said. In 1996, about $700 million went to domestic projects and $670 million went to foreign work, a company spokesman said.

For 1997, 67 percent of planned capital spending, or about $900 million, is directed to projects in Asia -- particularly Burma, Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines -- and crude oil projects in Azerbaijan.

Unocal said the greatest change in investment plan was the absence of refining and marketing projects due to the pending sale of its West Coast downstream assets to Tosco Corp for $2 billion. Capital spending for downstream refining, marketing and transportation in 1996 was about $205 million.
Unocal said it may increase spending with proceeds from the Tosco deal.

About $1.07 billion of the 1997 investment plan is directed toward worldwide petroleum exploration and production activities, up 19 percent from 1996. About $735 million is earmarked for foreign oil and gas activities, compared with nearly $495 million in 1996.

Unocal said it plans to expand its capital spending in Thailand and Indonesia in 1997. In Thailand, it plans to spend $220 million, up 34 percent from 1996, to develop additional natural gas production capacity to sustain production of more than one billion cubic feet per day.
In Indonesia, capital spending will increase 20 percent to $175 million. Unocal plans to develop new oil and gas discoveries offshore East Kalimantan.

In Burma, Unocal plans to spend nearly $140 million in 1997, up from $95 million in 1996, as its share of the development cost for the Yadana natural gas project, which is expected to be on line by mid-1998.
